:::caution[On main, next release]
This page was written from `main` at 1e8706a. These notes are for a release that is not out. HotLoop core 4.18.10 is the latest one you can install.
:::

HotLoop's database is PostgreSQL 17 from this release, and every install that has
PostgreSQL 16 data moves on its next upgrade without you running anything. That
is the one thing in 4.18.11 you need to read before you touch a running plant,
because it is a change of database engine, it needs disk, and there is one way
back that is not a plain rollback.

The full notes are in the README:
What changed in 4.18.11.

## PostgreSQL 17, and the upgrade that comes with it

- **What changed.** The database the charts and the Quadlet units run is
  PostgreSQL 17: TimescaleDB 2.30.1 on it for Edge and the Gateway, plain
  PostgreSQL 17.11 for IoT and for `database.type: postgresql`. SQLite installs
  have no PostgreSQL and are not touched. PostgreSQL will not open another major
  version's data directory, so a bare image change would have left every
  existing box with a database that cannot start. I wasn't willing to ship that.
- **What happens on the first start.** One script, `hotloop-pg-upgrade.sh`, runs
  before the database. On the chart it is two init containers on the database
  pod: the old image hands over its PostgreSQL 16 install and the new image runs
  `pg_upgrade`. On Quadlet it is `hotloop-db-upgrade.container`, a oneshot unit
  that `hotloop-db.container` requires. It works in copy mode into a new
  directory beside the old one, starts the new server once to prove it opens, and
  only then swaps the names. A fresh install, or a volume already on 17, does
  nothing.
- **Expect a wait.** The database pod sits in `Init` for as long as a copy of your
  data takes, and the app waits for it. The log is
  `kubectl logs <release>-postgresql-0 -c pg-upgrade` on the chart and
  `journalctl -u hotloop-db-upgrade` on Quadlet.
- **Free space.** It needs about as much free space beside the data as the data
  takes, and it checks before it starts. If there isn't room it stops, with the
  16 data exactly as it was and the database not started.
- **`pgdata.pg16` is kept, and it is yours to delete.** The old directory is
  renamed `pgdata.pg16` and left on the volume. It is the whole PostgreSQL 16
  database as it stood at the upgrade, which is the backup and the way back, and
  it is as big as the database. It stays until you remove it. When the box has
  run on 17 for as long as you want:

  ```sh
  # chart
  kubectl -n hotloop exec hotloop-postgresql-0 -c postgresql -- rm -rf /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata.pg16
  # Quadlet
  sudo rm -rf "$(sudo podman volume inspect hotloop-db --format '{{.Mountpoint}}')/pgdata.pg16"
  ```

- **A failure leaves you where you were.** If anything fails before the swap, the
  16 data is untouched and the database does not start on a half-built
  directory. On the chart the pod stays in `Init:Error`, on Quadlet the upgrade
  unit fails and the database unit behind it never starts. Fix what the log says
  and start it again.
- **`helm rollback` to 4.18.10 will not start its database.** This is the caveat.
  A rollback puts the chart's database image back to PostgreSQL 16, and 16 will
  not open a 17 directory. Nothing is lost and nothing is half changed, the
  database just does not start. Getting it back means the swap in
  docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:
  stop the database, move `pgdata` to `pgdata.pg17` and `pgdata.pg16` to
  `pgdata`. **That drops every write made on 17 since the upgrade**, because
  `pgdata.pg16` is the database as it was at that moment. Roll forward when you
  can. The swap-back only works once, and the next upgrade refuses to run while a
  `pgdata.pg16` is in the way.
- **Quadlet boxes aren't hit by that.** Podman's auto-update rolls back only the
  app, never the database, and the 4.18.10 app reads a PostgreSQL 17 database
  fine, because migrations only add. A Quadlet box that rolls an update back
  keeps running.
- **Take a backup first anyway.** HotLoop's own backup is made by the running app
  through the running database, so it can't be taken in the step that runs
  before the database starts. Take one on 4.18.10 before you upgrade and copy it
  off the box. Restoring it onto 17 is the ordinary restore.
- **Turning it off.** `database.postgresql.upgrade.enabled: false` drops the init
  containers, and a volume still on 16 then stops the database from starting.
  Leave it on. With it on, a fresh install still pulls the PostgreSQL 16 image
  once per node, because an init container's image is pulled before it runs.

### API changes

- **New routes:** `GET` and `PUT /api/notify/escalation`, and `GET
  /manifest.webmanifest` and `GET /sw.js`, which need no session because a phone
  asks before anybody has signed in. All in docs/API.md.
- **Integration routes:** `GET /api/integrations` (`devices.read`), and `POST
  /api/integrations/{id}/probe` and `/setup` (`devices.write`). No new permission.
- **Two new protocols,** `snmp` and `bacnet`, in `GET /api/protocols` and in the
  `no driver for protocol` error's list. HotLoop now speaks ten.
- **Kiosk and lockout routes:** `POST /api/auth/kiosk` (no session), `POST
  /api/auth/activity`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/users/{username}/pin` and `DELETE
  /api/users/{username}/lockout`, both under `users.manage`. `GET /api/users` says
  `hasPin` and `locked`, never the code. The login route answers `429` with a
  `Retry-After` for a locked account. A kiosk session reports `idleSec`. New
  settings `ui.kioskIdleSeconds`, `ui.lockoutAttempts`, `ui.lockoutSeconds` and
  `ui.panelDelaySeconds`.
- **New permission:** `notify.escalation`, admin only. The viewer and operator
  roles did not get it.
- **The alarm trail has two new event types,** `escalated` and `escalation-ended`,
  with `actor` set to `escalation`. A script that reads an alarm's history and
  assumes the old list will meet them.
- `GET /api/stream` closes when its session ends, and a history bucket's time
  is in UTC. Both are under "What else is in it".

### Upgrading from 4.18.10

- **Chart:** `helm upgrade <release> hotloop/hotloop --version 4.18.11
  --reset-then-reuse-values`, and the same for `hotloop-edge` and `hotloop-iot`.
  The database pod runs the upgrade first, as above.
- **Quadlet:** copy the new `hotloop-db.container`, `hotloop-db-upgrade.container`
  and `hotloop-db-upgrade.sh` from your product's directory in `deploy/quadlet/`
  into the units directory, run `systemctl daemon-reload`, and restart
  `hotloop-db.service`. The database unit requires the upgrade unit, so a box
  that only got the new database unit does not start on 16 data and says why.
  The PostgreSQL 16 image is pulled only when the volume needs it.
- **One new migration, `0025_kiosk_pin`,** for PostgreSQL and SQLite. It only adds
  columns (a PIN hash, a session's idle limit, and the lockout counters), every one
  with a default, so 4.18.10 runs on the schema it leaves. `pg_dump` first, like always.
- **Edge Relay:** no database and nothing to do. It ships at 4.18.11 because
  every product ships in lockstep.

### What else is in it

- **Integrations: point HotLoop at a device you know the address of.** One flow for
  every kind of device: ask what the integration needs, look at the real device
  with the answers, keep the points you want, and nothing it makes is armed.
  Every tag a setup makes is read-only, and a setup that fails part way leaves no
  device behind. OPC UA goes through it first. Why it matters: a new kind of
  device used to need its own screen and its own idea of what a setup does, and
  now adding one is the same three steps.
  docs/INTEGRATIONS.md.
- **SNMP, read-only.** Versions 1, 2c and 3 for switches, UPSs, PDUs, power meters
  and any Linux box running `snmpd`. HotLoop never sends a SET, because a SET can
  change a switch. There is no default community, since `public` is how a plant's
  switches get read by whoever asks. The community and the v3 passphrases are
  stored encrypted like every other device secret. Proven against net-snmp's
  agent in the lab at every v3 security level. **Not proven on a physical
  switch, UPS or PDU:** vendors differ on MIBs, interface numbering and bulk
  requests, so treat the first read of a real device as commissioning and compare
  the probe's sampled values with the device's own display.
- **BACnet/IP, read-only.** Building controllers and meters on the IP network:
  objects, units and status flags, with a device behind a router said to be
  unreachable instead of silently missing. HotLoop never writes a BACnet
  property, because a write lands on a priority array and a priority left set
  holds the equipment where it was put. The client is written for HotLoop from
  the standard and held to frames recorded off a device and to bacpypes3 in the
  lab. **Not proven on a physical controller,** and nothing on an MS/TP trunk
  behind a router can be reached.
  docs/PROTOCOLS.md.
- **Kiosk sign-in, and a lockout that is on by default.** A panel opened at
  `/?screen=<name>` asks for one field, a PIN or whatever a keyboard badge reader
  types, and every write through the gate is that person's, so the audit trail says
  who opened the valve instead of "panel-3". Left alone for 15 minutes it signs them
  out on the page and on the server, so a hung page can't leave a name signed in.
  An admin sets a code per account in Settings, Users, or over the API. Codes are
  bcrypt like passwords, six characters at least, one code opens one account. On
  your own computer nothing changes: you are signed in and a write goes straight
  through. **The behavior change to know about:** wrong passwords and PINs now lock
  the one account after 10 in a row for 5 minutes, and an admin can unlock it.
  That is on for every install, including ones that never use a kiosk. A script that
  retries a wrong password more than ten times will start getting `429`. Set
  `HOTLOOP_AUTH_LOCKOUT_ATTEMPTS=0` for no lockout. A wrong code typed alone locks
  no account, so it can't be used to lock the whole panel; the panel waits half a
  second longer per miss, up to 3 seconds, and is never locked. Not built: reading a
  badge from a reader that isn't a keyboard.
  docs/AUTH.md.
- **Alarm escalation.** An alarm nobody acknowledges now goes to the next
  person. Under Settings an admin edits a policy: people who have an ntfy topic
  or an address of their own, steps that say who is told after how many minutes,
  and a repeat. An acknowledgement from anywhere stops it, because the escalator
  asks the alarm engine before every send, and every step and every stop is a
  row in the alarm's own trail, so the logbook has it. A restart in the middle of
  a chain carries on from what the audit rows say went out. It is off until you
  turn it on, it needs `HOTLOOP_NOTIFY_ENABLED`, and it can only use the
  channels your deployment already has. Why it matters: a page to a phone on a
  nightstand used to be the end of it. It is proven against the lab's real ntfy,
  Gotify and Mailpit with a fake clock, not against a plant's phones.
  Details in docs/NOTIFY.md.
- **The UI installs on a phone and opens with no connection.** HotLoop serves a
  manifest, icons and a service worker. The phone keeps the page and the last
  answer to the reads a person looks at, a bar across the bottom says what time it
  is as of, and every write is refused before it leaves the page: the worker never
  answers, keeps or queues a write. Signing out empties what the phone kept. It
  only runs over https or `localhost`, so a plant on plain http gets the same UI as
  before. Why it matters: an old page that says it is old beats a blank one when
  the Wi-Fi drops in the one spot you needed it.
  docs/DASHBOARDS.md.
- **The live feed stops when its session does.** `GET /api/stream` looked at the
  session once, when it opened, and a stream stays open for hours, so it kept
  sending the plant's live data after a sign out, an expiry, a revoked session
  or a disabled account. It checks every five seconds now and closes when the
  session is gone, without counting the check as the session being used, so a
  screen left on a wall still goes idle. No route, field or permission changed.
- **A history bucket's time is written in UTC.** `HistoryBuckets` handed a
  bucket edge back in the box's own timezone, so the same trend spelled its
  times one way on a plant set to New York and another on a plant set to UTC.
  The edge is an instant, and it is the same instant either way. A script that
  compared the strings, not the times, will see the offset change.
- **Docs that were wrong in 4.18.10.** Four links and counts: the Edge Relay page
  linked a discovery anchor that was never the heading, the 4.18.10 notes linked
  a 4.18.4 anchor, and the MCP page said twenty-five tools over a table of
  twenty-seven, which is what the code registers. The README and the roadmap said
  IoT and Edge were coming next release, and they shipped in 4.18.10.

### What isn't proven

- **The upgrade is proven on 4.18.10 data,** for IoT, Edge and the Gateway, on
  the chart and on Quadlet, and `test/pgupgrade/run.sh` keeps it honest with the
  images that ship. How long it takes scales with your data, so watch the log
  the first time on a big one.
- **The swap back after a `helm rollback` is documented, not run by a test.**
  `test/pgupgrade/run.sh` checks the kept directory is a PostgreSQL 16 directory,
  and doesn't run the swap.
- **IoT's plain PostgreSQL directory has no TimescaleDB extension in it,** so the
  move up a product on a PostgreSQL 17 volume has not been run again on 17. It
  was run on 16 in 4.18.10.
- **Everything the 4.18.10 notes list as unproven** still is: Edge and IoT as live
  Quadlet units under systemd (except IoT's SQLite unit), a real Pi, and the
  32-bit arm images on real hardware.
